newsitem.title: USA: NYC gets $304 million of retail orders for bonds.
newsitem.headline: NYC gets $304 million of retail orders for bonds.

text.p: New York City got just over $304 million of orders from individual investors for $900 million of tax-exempt bonds that it is selling on Wednesday, a New York City official said on Tuesday.
The official, who declined to be named, said the city was checking to see whether this was a new record for retail orders during the presale period.

The official later said this was third biggest showing, as the record remained a March 1996 offering that drew over $335 million of orders from individual investors. That topped a November 1994 sale that attracted almost $315 million. The city had hoped to sell its usual volume of $150 million to $200 million in the presale period that ended at midday.

Traders speculated that the retail crowd's surging appetite for New York City bonds reflected concerns about the stock markets, which have staged a correction. The city official noted demand is concentrated at the short end of the yield curve. "A lot of it is that, there's enormous demand there for triple-tax-exempt, good return and short-term (debt). We sold out through 2004," he said. That was one more maturity closed than the city had anticipated on Monday, when it looked to sell out the five maturities from 1999 to 2003.

In the secondary market, traders said New York City's bonds have firmed over the past 18 months or so, reflecting views that the city's credit has improved with its finances. "Cities are trading at the most attractive levels they've been in a long time, on a gross yield basis," a trader said, noting they remained fairly costly when compared with Treasury bonds.

As part of the same offering, New York City on Wednesday also is selling through competition about $120 million of taxable debt. Another $50 million of variable-rate, short-term notes have been earmarked for European investors, who also prefer short-term maturities.
